questions.question: God chose men to write down His Words. What are these men called?
answers: Prophets. (2 Peter 1:20-21)

questions.question: How many years passed before all of God’s Word was written down?
answers: It took about 2,000 years before all of God’s words were written.

questions.question: How many men were there whom God used to write down His Word?
answers: About forty.

questions.question: Did they write God’s words in English?
answers: No. They were written in Hebrew, Greek, and Aramaic.

questions.question: Who is the author of the Bible?
answers: God. (2 Timothy 3:16)

questions.question: Why should a person study the Bible?
answers: The Bible is God’s personal message to every individual. (2 Peter 1:20-21)

questions.question: Was there ever a time when God was not living?
answers: No. (Psalm 90:2)

questions.question: What does God need in order to exist?
answers: Nothing. (Genesis 1:1)

questions.question: Does God have a body?
answers: No. (John 4:24)

questions.question: How many Gods are there?
answers: One God. (Mark 12:29-30)

questions.question: Who are the three persons who make the one God?
answers: God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit. (Matthew 28:19)

questions.question: Is there some faraway place you could go on this earth or in this galaxy or in this universe or anywhere that God would not be?
What do we mean when we say that God is sovereign?
answers: He is greater than all and more important than all; He is the highest in authority. (Isaiah 45:5)

questions.question: Who is the only One who lived before the beginning?
answers: God. (Genesis 1:1)

questions.question: Where did angels come from?
answers: They were created by God. (John 1:3)

questions.question: Did God create the angels with bodies of flesh and bones like us?
answers: No.

questions.question: Did God create good and bad angels?
answers: No, He made them all good. (1 Timothy 4:4)

questions.question: Why did God create angels?
answers: To be His servants. (Psalm 103:20-21)

questions.question: When they were first created, where did all the angels live?
answers: With God in Heaven. (Job 38:4–7)

questions.question: Who was the smartest and most beautiful angel God made?
answers: Lucifer. (Ezekiel 28:12)

questions.question: What special job did Lucifer get to have?
answers: He was made leader of all the other angels. (Ezekiel 28:14)

questions.question: What did Lucifer plan to do?
answers: He planned to be like God and take God's position. (Isaiah 14:13,14)

questions.question: Who else followed Lucifer in his rebellion against God?
answers: Many of God's angels. (Revelation 12:9)

questions.question: Did God know what Lucifer and the rebellious angels were planning?
answers: Yes. (Isaiah 14:13)

questions.question: What did God do?
answers: He removed Lucifer from his position and kicked Lucifer and the rebellious angels out of Heaven. (Isaiah 14:12-15, Revelation 12:7-9)

questions.question: Is there anything that God doesn't see, hear, and know?
answers: No! God sees, hears, and knows everything. (Proverbs 15:3)

questions.question: What place did God prepare as a punishment for Lucifer and the rebellious angels?
answers: The Lake of Fire. (Matthew 25:41)

questions.question: What new name did Lucifer get that means "enemy"?
answers: Satan. (1 Peter 5:8)

questions.question: Who is Satan's enemy? Who is he against?
answers: God. (John 8:44)

questions.question: Who, in the beginning, created the heavens and the earth?
answers: God. (Genesis 1:1)

questions.question: What did God use to make the heavens and the earth?
answers: God didn't use anything. He made everything out of nothing. (Psalm 33:6,9)

questions.question: Why was God able to make the heavens and the earth?
answers: God is all-powerful. Nothing is too hard for Him. (Jeremiah 32:17)

questions.question: How did God know how to make the heavens and the earth?
answers: God knows everything and He is all-powerful. (Proverbs 3:19-20)

questions.question: Who taught God how to make everything?
answers: No one taught God. (Jeremiah 10:12)

questions.question: Is there any person or any angel who knows everything like God does?
answers: No. Only God knows everything. (Romans 11:33-34)

questions.question: What was the earth like before God began to prepare it for people to live in?
answers: It was without form and in total darkness; no land and no life. (Genesis 1:2)

questions.question: What did God do in order to create everything?
answers: He spoke and commanded that things appear. (Hebrews 11:3)

questions.question: Why was God able to command the ocean to go back and stay where He wanted it?
answers: Because He is all-powerful and He created the ocean. (Psalm 95:5)

questions.question: Why did God create everything beautiful and why did He make all different kinds of fruit and vegetables to eat?
answers: He made them because He is loving and kind. He prepared everything for us. (Psalm 104:14–15)

questions.question: What did God say about all the things which He created?
answers: God said that they were good. (Genesis 1:4,10,12,18)

questions.question: How was God able to create such a big universe, with so many stars, so far apart?
answers: God is all-powerful and He is everywhere, all the time. (Jeremiah 10:12)

questions.question: When you see designs and patterns and repeated shapes in flowers and trees and all living things, what does that remind you of?
answers: The fact that God is the Master Designer – the Creator of everything. (Romans 1:20)

questions.question: What did God say about all the things which He created?
answers: God said that they were good. (Genesis 1:4,10,12,18,21,25)

questions.question: Why was God able to create all the things perfect?
answers: Because He is perfect. (Psalm 18:30)

questions.question: How was God able to create so many kinds of birds and sea creatures?
answers: God is all-powerful and all-knowing. (Psalm 104:24–25)

questions.question: When you see designs and patterns in living things, what does that remind you of?
answers: The fact that God is the Master Designer – the Creator of everything. (Romans 1:20)

questions.question: Why did God make many different birds and fish?
answers: To show His love, wisdom, and power in creation. (1 Timothy 6:17)

questions.question: Who did God prepare the earth for?
answers: For man. (Psalm 115:16)

questions.question: What great difference was there between the creation of man and the creation of the animals?
answers: God created man in His image. (Genesis 1:26)

questions.question: What does it mean to be made in His image?
answers: To be made in the image of God means to be made to be like Him.

questions.question: What three things did God give man because man was made in His image?
answers: God gave man a mind so he can know God, emotions so he can love God, and a will so he can choose to obey God. (Mark 12:30)

questions.question: Who is the father of all people?
answers: Adam. (Acts 17:26)

questions.question: What special job did God give to Adam?
answers: To be manager over all the earth. (Genesis 1:28-30)

questions.question: What did God say everything was like at the beginning?
answers: Everything was very good. It was perfect! (Genesis 1:31)

questions.question: Does God ever begin a thing and then not finish it?
answers: No. (Isaiah 46:10-11)

questions.question: Why doesn't God begin things and leave them unfinished?
answers: Because God never changes, He always does what He says and nothing can keep Him from doing what He plans. (Isaiah 55:8-11)

questions.question: Why did God rest on the seventh day?
answers: Because His work of creating was done. (Genesis 2:2)

questions.question: Who did God plant the garden of Eden for?
answers: Adam. (Genesis 2:8)

questions.question: Why was it right for God to put Adam in the garden even though He didn't ask Adam if he wanted to live there?
answers: God created Adam, so he rightfully belongs to God. (Psalm 100:3)

questions.question: To whom do all things in the universe belong?
answers: To God, the Creator of everything. (Psalm 24:1)

questions.question: How many trees in the garden was Adam allowed to eat from?
answers: From all of them except one, the tree of knowledge of good and evil. (Genesis 2:9)

questions.question: What would happen to Adam if he ate from the tree of knowledge of good and evil?
answers: He would die or be separated. (Genesis 2:16-17)

questions.question: What would Adam be separated from?
answers: He would be separated from God, from his body, and forever in the Lake of Fire. (Romans 6:23)

questions.question: Who decided that Adam needed a wife?
answers: God decided. (Genesis 2:18)

questions.question: Why did God decide to make a wife for Adam?
answers: Because God loved Adam and did not want him to be alone. (Genesis 2:18)

questions.question: Was it right for God to decide to do this without asking Adam?
answers: Yes, God created Adam and he belongs to God. (Genesis 2:7)

questions.question: How did God make the first woman?
answers: God put Adam to sleep. He took out one of Adam’s ribs and then made the first woman from it. (Genesis 2:21-22)

questions.question: How was it possible for God to make Eve from Adam’s rib?
answers: God is all-powerful and can do anything He wants to. (Jeremiah 32:17)

questions.question: Who told Adam and Eve to marry and to have children?
answers: God, their Creator. (Genesis 1:28)

questions.question: When Satan came to deceive Eve, did he come to talk to her face-to-face so she could see him and know who he was?
answers: No. (Genesis 3:1-2)

questions.question: What did Satan use to disguise himself when he spoke to Eve?
answers: A snake. (Genesis 3:1)

questions.question: God told Adam that, if they ate the fruit from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, they would definitely die, but Satan told Eve they would not. What was Satan saying about God?
answers: That He is a liar. (John 8:44)

questions.question: Does Satan want you to believe God?
answers: No. (2 Corinthians 4:4)

questions.question: Adam and Eve didn’t immediately drop dead when they ate the fruit. God had said they would die for their disobedience. What did He mean?
answers: They would immediately be separated from God and their relationship with God would end. (Isaiah 59:2)
Their bodies would eventually die because of their disobedience and then they would be separated forever in the Lake of Fire. (Romans 6:23)

questions.question: What did Adam and Eve do when they heard God coming to see them?
answers: They hid because they were ashamed and afraid. (Genesis 3:8)

questions.question: Is it possible to hide from God?
answers: No. God is everywhere. (Hebrews 4:13)

questions.question: Did God call Adam because God didn’t know where Adam and Eve were?
answers: No, God knew where they were. God wanted them to come on their own and admit their sin. (Proverbs 28:13)

questions.question: Can anyone hide from God?
answers: No, God sees us all the time, no matter where we are. (Hebrews 4:13)

questions.question: Why did God have the right to call Adam and question him?
answers: Because God was Adam’s Creator and they belonged to God. (Romans 9:20-21)

questions.question: Why does God have the right to demand obedience?
answers: Because He gave life to everyone. (1 Timothy 6:13)

questions.question: What was God's curse on the snake?
answers: From that time, it was to move by crawling on its belly. (Genesis 3:14)

questions.question: Who did God promise to send?
answers: A Savior. (Genesis 3:15)

questions.question: Why did God promise to send a Savior?
answers: Because God loves all people. (Psalm 145:8)

questions.question: Did Adam and Eve deserve God’s love and promise of a Savior?
answers: No, they deserved everlasting punishment. (Romans 6:23)

questions.question: Who are the parents of all people?
answers: Adam and Eve. (Genesis 3:20)

questions.question: Why do all people have to die?
answers: Because Adam disobeyed God, all Adam’s descendants die. (Romans 5:12)

questions.question: Why did God refuse the clothes which Adam and Eve made?
answers: Because God wanted to show them that they can’t do anything themselves to fix things and make themselves acceptable to Him. (Ephesians 2:8-9)

questions.question: Is there anything that anyone can do themselves to be acceptable to God?
answers: No. (Romans 9:16)

questions.question: What are some of the things people might do to try to make themselves acceptable to God? Will God accept any of these?
answers: No. (Isaiah 64:6)

questions.question: Who is the only one that can make Adam and Eve acceptable to God?
answers: God. (Romans 8:3)

questions.question: Why did God kill animals to make clothing for Adam and Eve?
answers: Because God was reminding Adam and Eve that the punishment for sin is death. (Romans 6:23)

questions.question: Why did God put them outside the garden of Eden?
answers: So that they didn’t eat from the tree of life and then live forever. (Genesis 2:22-23)

questions.question: What did God put at the edge of the garden to keep Adam and Eve out?
answers: He put angels called cherubim and a sword of fire that flashed every direction. (Genesis 3:24)

questions.question: Where were Cain and Abel born?
answers: Outside the garden. (Genesis 3:34-4:2)

questions.question: Why were Cain and Abel born separated from God?
answers: Because Adam is their father. (Romans 5:12)

questions.question: Why are we born separated from God?
answers: Because Adam is our father. (Psalm 51:5)

questions.question: What did Cain and Abel bring to God when they came to worship Him?
answers: Cain brought some of the fruit from the ground, and Abel brought a lamb. (Genesis 4:3-5)

questions.question: Which offering did God accept?
answers: Abel’s offering. (Genesis 4:4)

questions.question: Why did God accept Abel's offering?
answers: Abel believed God, trusting that God would keep His promise to someday send a Savior, and came to God His way with a blood sacrifice. (Hebrews 11:4)

questions.question: Why did God reject Cain’s offering?
answers: Cain did not believe God, he did not trust that God would send a Savior, and came to God his own way, disregarding what God’s instructions. (Hebrews 11:4,6)

questions.question: Why did God talk to Cain about his choice?
answers: Because God loved Cain and wanted him to change his mind about doing it his own way and bring the correct sacrifice. (2 Peter 3:9)

questions.question: Did Cain believe and agree with God?
answers: No. (Genesis 4:8)

questions.question: What did Cain do after God rejected his offering?
answers: He became angry and killed Abel. (Genesis 4:8)

questions.question: How did God know what Cain had done?
answers: God sees and knows everything. (Hebrews 4:13)

questions.question: Why did God give another son, Seth, to Adam and Eve?
answers: God gave Seth as a replacement for Abel, so that the coming Savior could be born in his family line. (Genesis 4:25)

questions.question: What was the attitude of the people in Noah’s day?
answers: They were selfish, always fighting, and lying, and hurting others. They were not interested in knowing or pleasing God. (Genesis 6:5,11)

questions.question: What did God say He was going to do because the people wouldn’t repent?
answers: God said He would destroy all living things on the earth. (Genesis 6:6,7)

questions.question: Did Noah deserve to be saved from God’s punishment?
answers: No, He was a sinner and deserved to be punished with the other people. (Romans 3:23)

questions.question: Why did God save Noah?
answers: Because Noah agreed with God that he was a sinner and trusted God to save him through the coming Savior God promised to send. (Genesis 6:7,8)

questions.question: What did God tell Noah to do?
answers: God told him to build an ark. (Genesis 6:14)

questions.question: Did God allow Noah to build the ark however he wanted to?
answers: No, it had to be exactly as God commanded. (Genesis 6:14-16)

questions.question: What one important thing should be remember about the ark?
answers: There was only one door. There was only one way to enter the ark and be saved from judgment. (Genesis 6:16)

questions.question: What else did Noah do while he was building the ark?
answers: He was telling the people God's message and warning them that God was going to make it rain and the whole earth would be destroyed by a flood. (1 Peter 3:20)

questions.question: Did the people accept what Noah said and change their minds?
answers: No, they refused to believe. (2 Peter 2:5)

questions.question: How long did God wait for the people in Noah’s time to agree with Him?
answers: 120 years. (Genesis 6:3)

questions.question: How did those saved from judgment get into the ark?
answers: They all entered by the one door God told Noah to put on the ark. (Genesis 7:16)

questions.question: Why did God shut the door?
answers: To keep all those inside the ark safe from the flood. (Genesis 7:16,23)

questions.question: Did anyone outside the ark escape death?
answers: No, they all died. (Genesis 7:21-23)

questions.question: What sign did God give to show He would never again destroy the earth by a flood?
answers: The rainbow. (Genesis 9:12, 13)

questions.question: Does God keep his promises?
answers: Yes, God is true to His Word. He never lies. He never changes. (Numbers 23:19)

questions.question: Did the people who were later born from Noah’s family worship God?
answers: No, they followed their own ideas and worshiped the sun, moon, and stars instead of God, their Creator. (Romans 1:18-32)

questions.question: What was the reason the people had for wanting to build the tower of Babel?
answers: So they would not be scattered all over the world and so they could be important. (Genesis 11:4)

questions.question: Did God know what they planned to do?
answers: Yes, God knows everything. (Genesis 11:5, Proverbs 15:3)

questions.question: What did God do to stop the building of the tower?
answers: He gave different languages to different families so that they could no longer understand each other, forcing them to stop building. (Genesis 11:6-9)

questions.question: What happened after the people stopped building the tower of Babel?
answers: The people moved away, spreading all over the earth. (Genesis 11:9)

questions.question: Did God abandon His plan to send a Savior for mankind because they rebelled against God and built the tower of Babel?
answers: No. God always does what He says; He never changes. (Numbers 23:19)

questions.question: What did God tell Abram to do?
answers: God told him to leave his own country and go to the place God promised to lead him to. (Genesis 12:1)

questions.question: How many children did Abram and Sarai have when God told Abram to go into a different country?
answers: They didn’t have any children. (Genesis 11:30)

questions.question: What things did God promise Abram?
answers: ⛰️ Land — God told Abram that He would give him the land of Canaan. (Genesis 12:1)
👥 Huge Family — God said that Abram’s family would become so great they would be a nation. (Genesis 12:2)
☂️ Protection — God said he would protect and prosper Abram so that he would be an important man and through him others would benefit. (Genesis 12:3)
🛟 Savior — God also said that all the world would be helped by the Savior God would send in Abram’s family line. (Genesis 12:3)

questions.question: God spoke directly to Abram. How does God talk to us today?
answers: Through His Word, the Bible. (2 Timothy 3:16–17)

questions.question: Did God choose Abram because he wasn’t a sinner?
answers: No, all people are sinners. (Romans 3:23)

questions.question: What did Abram do when God made him these promises?
answers: He believed God. He left his home country and went where God showed him to go. (Genesis 12:4)

questions.question: Why did Lot move away from Abram and live near Sodom and Gomorrah?
answers: Abram and Lot had so many animals that there wasn’t enough grass and space for them both to live together. (Genesis 13:5-7)
Lot moved to the plain because it was well-watered and had much more grass for his animals. (Genesis 13:10-11)

questions.question: What did God promise Abram after he left his home area, his father died, and now Lot left him?
answers: God told Abram that He would give him the land of Canaan. (Genesis 13:14,15)

questions.question: What did God promise Abram about his family?
answers: God promised that Abram’s family would number more than the stars. (Genesis 15:5)

questions.question: What did God say would happen to Abram’s family in the future?
answers: God said that Abram’s family would go live in another country and that they would be treated badly for 400 years, but after that they would leave with great possessions, come back to Canaan, and the land God promised would be theirs. (Genesis 15:13-16)

questions.question: What new names did God give to Abram and Sarai?
answers: Abraham and Sarah. (Genesis 17:5,15)

questions.question: Why would it take a miracle from God for Abraham and Sarah to have a child?
answers: Sarah was unable to have a child. (Genesis 11:30)
They were too old. Abraham was now 100 years old and Sarah was 90. (Genesis 17:17)

questions.question: Who created the first man and woman and gives life to every baby?
answers: God. (Nehemiah 9:6)

questions.question: Is there anything which God wants to do but cannot?
answers: No, God can do everything He wants to do. (Psalm 135:6)

questions.question: Who knows the future of every person?
answers: Only God. (Psalm 139:4,16)

questions.question: Who knows the future of every person?
answers: Only God. (Psalm 139:16)

questions.question: Did God know about all the wickedness of Sodom and Gomorrah?
answers: Yes. (Genesis 18:20-21)

questions.question: If people ignore God, will He overlook their sin and not punish them?
answers: No, God will judge every person. (Hebrews 4:13)

questions.question: Why didn’t God immediately punish the evil people of Sodom and Gomorrah, and why doesn’t God immediately punish sinners now?
answers: Because God is loving, merciful, gracious, and patient. He gives people time to change their minds and trust in Him. (2 Peter 3:9)

questions.question: Does God just threaten but never actually do it?
answers: No, even though God is patient, He will eventually punish sinners. (Ezekiel 24:14)

questions.question: Can anyone stop God from punishing people when He decides it is time?
answers: No, God is supreme. No one is greater than He is. (Psalm 86:8)

questions.question: Why did the Lord send His angels to rescue Lot, his wife, and his family?
answers: Because Lot agreed with God that he was a sinner and trusted in God’s promises to send a Savior. (2 Peter 2:7–9)

questions.question: Why did God turn Lot’s wife into a pillar of salt?
answers: Because she disobeyed the Lord’s command that they must not look back at the burning cities. (Genesis 19:17,26)

questions.question: Why was God able to give Abraham and Sarah a son even though he was 100 years old and she was 90?
answers: Because God gives life to all people everywhere. (Job 12:10)
God is able to do anything He wants to do. (Jeremiah 32:17)

questions.question: What authority did God have to ask Abraham to offer Isaac as a sacrifice?
answers: God is the Creator of all things and He owns all things. (Psalm 89:11)
God gave life to Isaac. (Psalm 100:3)

questions.question: Did Abraham think that God had changed his mind about giving Abraham a big family and sending a Savior through Isaac?
answers: No, Abraham believed and trusted in God because he was convinced that God always keeps His promises. (Genesis 22:8)

questions.question: What did Abraham think God might do?
answers: Abraham thought that if he did kill Isaac as God had commanded him, then God would raise Isaac from the dead. (Hebrews 11:17–19)

questions.question: Once Abraham had tied up Isaac and put him on the altar was there any way Isaac could save himself from death?
answers: No, Isaac could not save himself from death. (Genesis 22:9)

questions.question: Is there any one who can save themselves from the payment of death that their sins deserve?
answers: No, no one can save himself or herself from the punishment of God. No one can escape from God. (Hebrews 4:13)

questions.question: Who provided a sacrifice to take Isaac’s place?
answers: God did. (Genesis 22:13)

questions.question: Why did Abraham call the place where God provided the ram, “The Lord will provide”?
answers: Because Abraham believed that, just as the Lord provided the ram instead of Isaac, the Lord would one day provide the Savior who would overcome Satan and deliver all people from Satan’s power and everlasting punishment. (Genesis 22:14)

questions.question: What was the big differenece between Esau and Jacob?
answers: Esau did not value God's promises given to Abraham concerning the Savior. Esau did not admit he was a sinner and trust in God's mercy. Esau lived for the present and for material gain. (Genesis 25:34, Hebrews 12:16)
Jacob admitted that he was a sinner and trusted in God. Jacob valued the promises concerning the Savior. (Hebrews 11:20,21)

questions.question: Why didn't God forget His promises about the Savior given to Adam and Eve in the garden of Eden and to Abraham?
answers: God didn't forget because He is unchanging and He always does what He says. (James 1:17)

questions.question: What did Jacob see in the dream given to him by God?
answers: He saw a stairway restong on the earth with its top reaching to Heaven. God's angels were walking up and down the ladder, and God stood above the ladder. (Genesis 28:12)

questions.question: What did this dream mean?
answers: It meant that the Savior, who would be the descendant of Jacob, would be like the stairway connecting the earth to Heaven. Therough the Savior, people could be brought back into oneness with God. (Genesis 28:13-15)

questions.question: God spoke to Jacob in dream. How does God speak to people today?
answers: God speaks to people today through His Word, the Bible. (2 Timothy 3:16-17)

questions.question: Who was Jacob's favorite son?
answers: Joseph (Genesis 37:3)

questions.question: How did Joseph's brothers feel about their father's love for Joseph?
answers: They were jealous, and they hated Joseph. (Genesis 37:4)

questions.question: What did Joseph dream about?
answers: Joseph dreamed about his family bowing down to him, first represented by bundles of crops (his brothers' sheaves bowing to his sheaf) and then by the sun, the moon, and 11 stars bending down in respect. (Genesis 37:7-9)

questions.question: What did these dreams mean?
answers: They meant that Joseph would one day be given a position of authority over his family. (Genesis 37:8, 10; 42:6; 43:26)

questions.question: Who knew Joseph's future and showed it to him through his dreams?
answers: God did. (Psalm 139:1-4)

questions.question: How much of our future does God know?
answers: God knows all things, including our future. (Psalm 139:15-16)

questions.question: What did Joseph's older brothers do to him?
answers: They sold Joseph to become a slave in Egypt. (Genesis 37:18-28)

questions.question: What happened to Joseph in Egypt?
answers: The wife of Joseph's owner lied about him, and he was put into prison. (Genesis 39:11-20)

questions.question: Who took care of Joseph in prison?
answers: God did. (Genesis 39:21)

questions.question: Why did God take care of Joseph?
answers: Because, although Joseph was a sinner, he trusted God and His mercy. (Psalm 105:17-19)
Because Joseph believed God's promises regarding the Savior. (Hebrews 11:22)
Because God had a wonderful plan for Joseph's life. (Jeremiah 29:11)

questions.question: Who gave Joseph the understanding of Pharaoh's dreams?
answers: God did. (Genesis 41:25)

questions.question: What did Pharaoh's dreams mean?
answers: God was making known to the king that there would be seven years of very good harvest which would be followed by seven years of drought. (Genesis 41:26-31)

questions.question: Is God able to do whatever He wants to do, even in places where the people do not know or worship Him?
answers: Yes, God is able to do whatever He wants to do, for He is almighty. (Daniel 4:35)

questions.question: How did God fulfill the dreams which He had given to Joseph when he was a young man?
answers: The Lord gave Joseph wisdom to interpret the king's dreams so that Joseph would be given the position next to the king. (Genesis 41:38-41)

questions.question: Why did Jacob take all of his family down to live in Egypt?
answers: Because Jacob had heard that Joseph was in Egypt. (Genesis 45:28)
Because there was plenty of food in Egypt. (Genesis 42:2)
Because the king invited Jacob to live in Egypt. (Genesis 45:17-20)
Because God had planned for this to happen. (Genesis 46:3-4)

questions.question: What were Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob's descendants called?
answers: The children of Israel, Israelites, or Israel. (Genesis 32:28; 46:8)

questions.question: Why did the king of Egypt make the Israelites slaves?
answers: Because they had become more in number than the Egyptians, the king was afraid that the Israelites might join with the Egyptian's enemies to fight against them and take control of Egypt. (Exodus 1:8-11)

questions.question: Who was guiding the king in his wicked plans?
answers: Satan. (1 Peter 5:8)

questions.question: Why would Satan wish to destroy the Israelites?
answers: Satan knew that God had promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that one of their descendants would be the Savior. (Genesis 12:3)

questions.question: Why did the Lord allow Pharaoh's daughter to adopt Moses?
answers: Because God planned to use Moses to deliver the Israelites from slavery. (Acts 7:20-22)

questions.question: Could the Israelites save themselves from slavery or could Moses save them?
Who is the only One who can save a person from Satan's control?
answers: God. (2 Timothy 2:25-26)

questions.question: Why did God decide to save the Israelites from slavery?
answers: Because the Lord saw their suffering and heard their cries. (Exodus 2:24)
Because God loved them and planned to reveal His love and mercy to them. (Deuteronomy 4:37)
Because the Lord had promised Abraham that He would make Abraham's descendants into a great nnnation and that, through them, the Savior would come into the world. (Deuteronomy 7:7-8)

questions.question: Why was the bush whch Moses saw not being burned up, even though it was in flames?
answers: The bush was not burned up because the Almighty God was in the bush. (Exodus 3:2-3)

questions.question: What does the name of God, "I AM," mean?
answers: It means that God doesn't need anything or anyone. He was there before the beginning of all things. Because He is the Creator of all things, everything is under His power, and He is totally independent of all things. (Exodus 3:14, Revelation 1:8)

questions.question: Did God think that the king of Egypt would release the Israelites immediately when Moses told him what the Lord had said?
answers: No, He knew the the king would not free the Israelites until he had to. God knows everything. (Exodus 3:19; 4:21)

questions.question: How did God plan to use the wicked Pharaoh?
answers: God planned to use this proud king to show everyone that the God of Israel is the only true and living God and that He is almighty. (Romans 9:17)

questions.question: How did the Lord show His power?
answers: The Lord sent great and terrible plagues on the Egyptians. (Exodus 7:5; 9:14-16; 14:4)

questions.question: Why didn't these plagues also come on the Israelites?
answers: Because of the Lord's love and grace. (Deuteronomy 7:7-8)
Because God had not forgotten His promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that He would make their descendants into a great nation and that He would be their God. (Deuteronomy 4:37)
So that the Egyptians would realize that the God of Israel was the only true and living God in the whole earth. (Exodus 10:1-2)

questions.question: Did the Israelites deserve to be protected like this?
answers: No, they, too, were sinners and deserved God's judgement. (Deuteronomy 9:4-6)

questions.question: What was the last plague which God sent on the Egyptians?
answers: God sent a plague which killed the firstborn in every Egyptian family and the firstborn of all their livestock. (Exodus 11:4-5; 12:12-13)

questions.question: What did God tell the Israelites to do so their firstborn children would not die?
answers: They must choose a lamb without blemish. (Exodus 12:5)
They must kill the lamb and catch its blood in a basin. (Exodus 12:22)
They must put the blood on the doorposts and above the door. (Exodus 12:7)
They must stay inside the house where the blood was placed. (Exodus 12:22-23)
They must not break any of the lambs bones. (Exodus 12:46)

questions.question: What would have happened if the Israelites had not done everything exactly as God instructed Moses?
answers: Their firstborn children would also have died. (Exodus 12:13, 22-23)

questions.question: Who is the only One who can tell us how we can come to God and be accepted by Him?
answers: God. (Proverbs 3:5-6)

questions.question: What happened in the Egyptians homes on the night when God said that He would kill the firstborn of every family?
answers: God killed them, just as He said He would. (Exodus 12:29-30)

questions.question: What was God's promise to the Israelites?
answers: God promised them that when He saw the blood on the doorposts and over their doors, He would pass over them. (Exodus 12:13, 23)

questions.question: What happened to the Israelites?
answers: All of their children were safe. None of them died. (Exodus 12:27-28)

questions.question: What did Pharaoh, the king, tell Moses after the Egyptians' firstborn children died?
answers: Pharaoh told Moses to take all the Israelites out of Egypt. (Exodus 12:31-32)

questions.question: How did the Lord show the Israelites where to go?
answers: God led them by a cloud during the day, and by a pillar of fire at night. (Exodus 13:17,18)

questions.question: To which land were the Israelites heading?
answers: To Canaan, the land God promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. (Genesis 13:14,15)

questions.question: Why did God protect Israel?
answers: Because He is loving and merciful. (Psalm 136:10-15)
Because one of their descendants was to be the Savior. (Isaiah 9:6-7)
Because of His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. (Genesis 12:3, Genesis 26:3-4, Genesis 28:14)
Because He was giving His Word to Israel to give to the world. (Isaiah 49:6)

questions.question: What did the Israelites do when they saw Pharaoh's armies coming behind them?
answers: They blamed Moses and said they should have left them in Egypt. (Exodus 14:10-12)

questions.question: Was there any way the Israelites could save themselves?
answers: No. (Exodus 14:11-12)

questions.question: What should they have done?
answers: They should have called on the Lord and trusted Him to rescue them. (Psalm 107:6)

questions.question: Why wasn't it difficult for God to open up the sea?
answers: Because He created the sea. (Psalm 95:5)
Because God is almighty. Nothing is too hard for Him. (Jeremiah 32:17)

questions.question: What did God do to protect the Israelites from the Egyptians when they were walking through the sea?
answers: God placed the cloud behind the Israelites so it was between them and the Egyptians. The cloud shone brightly to show the way for the Israelites, but it was a dark, black cloud in front of the Egyptians. (Exodus 14:19-22)

questions.question: Why couldn't the Egyptians escape from God?
answers: Because the Lord is creater than all. No one can fight agaist Him and win. He is almighty. (Proverbs 21:30)

questions.question: Can anyone make a way to save themself from God's punishment for their sins and make themselves acceptable to God?
answers: No. (Romans 3:23)

questions.question: What new problem did the Israelites face after God saved them from the Egyptian army at the Red Sea and began their journey through the wilderness?
answers: They didn't have any food. (Exodus 16:3)

questions.question: Did the Israelites remember all the great thing God had done, and did they trust in Him?
answers: No, they complained and blamed Moses and Aaron. (Exodus 16:2)

questions.question: Did Israel deserve to be given food by God?
answers: No. (Deuteronomy 9:6)

questions.question: Is there any person who deserves God's love or deserves to be saved from everlasting punishment?
answers: No, we all deserve to be punished by God. (Romans 3:23)

questions.question: What did God tell Moses to do in order to provide water?
answers: He had to hit the rock with his stick. (Exodus 17:5,6)

questions.question: When God saved the Israelites, did He allow them to do things the way they wanted to do it?
answers: No, they had to do it God's way. (Acts 4:12)

questions.question: Why did God protect and provide for Israel?
answers: Because He is loving and merciful. (Psalm 136:10-15)
Because one of their descendants was to be the Savior. (Isaiah 9:6-7)
Because of His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. (Genesis 12:3, Genesis 26:3-4, Genesis 28:14)
Because He was giving His Word to Israel to give to the world. (Isaiah 49:6)

questions.question: Was there any way the Israelites could provide food or water for themselves?
answers: No. (Deuteronomy 8:3)

questions.question: What should they have done?
answers: They should have called on the Lord and trusted Him to provide for them. (Psalm 50:15)
